status: proposed contract handoffs; no story implementation or approval asserted
source: Current DEF proposed story scope and implementation roadmap TU1 ordered steps

stories.title: Distinguish and reconcile immutable usage observations

functionalRequirements.statement: Identify logical requests, actual attempts, source granularity, model identity and charged ownership without treating references or transport delivery as new consumption.
Resolve observations conservatively while preserving every original fact and disclosing uncertainty, conflicts and explicit ownership changes.

stories.title: Persist root and descendant usage in a recoverable Avro ledger

functionalRequirements.statement: Append root and descendant events to one root Avro container through a serialized daemon writer, with durable acknowledgment, duplicate detection and interrupted-tail recovery.

Implement usage-root resolution using canonical identities, ownership links and explicit dispatch bindings, including standalone and pre-content root/child reservations. Never infer roots from missing links or copy usage into artifact JSON.

stories.title: Keep usage independent of artifact lifecycle and reconcile ledger transfers

functionalRequirements.statement: Keep artifact writes separate from the root ledger while preserving history through paired import/export, supersession, deletion/retention and binary-safe branch reconciliation.
Keep observational freshness separate from content revision, approval and signoff while exposing legacy and unsupported evidence honestly.

stories.title: Provide daemon accounting access and operational guarantees

functionalRequirements.statement: Provide daemon-owned artifact-level submission and reading with explicit acceptance, recovery, conflict and unsupported-version outcomes.
Expose root watermarks, bounded record access and committed report snapshots consumable by the daemon DuckDB query layer, without requiring hierarchical reporting implementation in TU1.

rationale.s2: Durable submissions need s1 stable IDs, immutable event schema and dedup/reconciliation semantics before persistence can validate a record.
rationale.s3: Lifecycle/import/transfer behavior operates on s2 acknowledged root ledgers and stable reserved owners; s2 must exist first.
rationale.s4: Daemon submission/read and operational qualification expose the s2 storage contract and the s3 independent lifecycle/transfer guarantees. Full hierarchical SQL belongs to TU4.
